coverage: All 25 PNGs individually inspected using view_image. No source, keys, mappings or other review files read.
recognition: Tentative StarCraft II recognition in view15, Company of Heroes in views02/24, and recognizable tactical planning scenes01/04 without confident exact title. Visually unchanged anchors retain identical prior scores.

view-01.png.evidence: Thick walls, furniture, distinct floors and warm/cool room lighting create clear spatial depth. Tiny figures and thin planning paths require scrutiny.

view-02.png.evidence: Fog, ruins, foliage, tracks and smoke create layered battlefield depth. Small camouflaged units merge into the detailed terrain.

view-03.png.evidence: Service yard with tracks, parked objects and fencing adds a distinct functional zone beside the airfield; subdued trees and varied grass support the military setting. Soft rendering blurs small props; plane overlaps a hangar and regular shoreline stones remain formulaic.

view-04.png.evidence: Produce stalls, carts, warm light and grounded shadows create coherent market space. Planning paths stand apart, but people and icons are small and crowded.

view-05.png.evidence: Continuous tan planked deck and raised island establish the carrier, with a long wake adding motion. Soft wing edges and pale deck reduce contrast where aircraft overlap; broad uniform tan surface reads flatter than a more materially separated deck.

view-06.png.evidence: Crisp hangar walls, shadows, fenced service yard, parked equipment and tracks give the airfield meaningful structure and varied materials. Player edging helps against roofs but still overlaps one; repeating rocks, identical hangars and uniformly straight beach limit naturalism.

view-07.png.evidence: Pale player outline separates the aircraft from olive terrain, and subdued trees with shadows cohere with the coast. Only a fragment of the new yard is visible; broad grass and regular stones still dominate and soft rendering weakens small detail.

view-08.png.evidence: Shaded trees, rocks, raised hangars and warm mottled grass give the airfield context. Plane overlaps hangar, edges are soft, and regular shoreline stones and blank open ground remain.

view-09.png.evidence: Sharp planked deck, raised island, narrow hull rim and long wake keep the carrier coherent. Pale aircraft lose some separation on the now lighter continuous deck; player still merges with stern and small deck marks crowd silhouettes.

view-10.png.evidence: Dark border and planked center distinguish deck materials; long twin wake conveys motion. Soft resolution, broad flat dark bow and player-stern overlap remain.

view-11.png.evidence: Sharp planked center, dark hull and long wake provide clear surface and motion cues. Broad dark bow is flat and the player overlaps the stern; fine fittings do not supply rich lighting.

view-12.png.evidence: Sharp planked deck and dark hull border improve material definition with restrained whitecaps and long wake. Dense aircraft and soft dot particles conceal player and compete with deck marks.

view-13.png.evidence: Open layout and objectives keep plane visible; olive mottling and pale fields add surface variety. Soft rendering, repeated stones and largely empty terrain limit richness.

view-14.png.evidence: Crisp planks and dark hull sides add materials; long wake restores motion. Aircraft overlap markings, player merges with stern, and aircraft height remains weakly expressed.

view-15.png.evidence: Luminous impact, sparks and beams create a strong focal event among detailed ships and terrain. Dark clustered units merge and the blast hides targets.

view-16.png.evidence: Open composition, sharp continuous planked deck and long wake make the carrier easy to parse. Narrow dark hull edge supports silhouette, but lighter broad deck gives less material separation; stern-player overlap persists.

view-17.png.evidence: Sparse carrier and fixed objectives stay readable, with tan deck, shaded island and long wake. Soft fittings and fairly uniform deck lighting limit depth; player still overlaps stern.

view-18.png.evidence: Dark carrier rim, planked deck and long wake add surface and motion cues. Soft aircraft edges, deck overlap and flat dark bow limit polish.

view-19.png.evidence: Sharp hangars and shadows ground the airfield; warmer grass and rocks add materials. Mottling adds few landmarks, plane overlaps roof, and shore lacks surf.

view-20.png.evidence: Textured deck and dark hull distinguish carrier from water; long wake indicates motion. Soft aircraft, particles and deck marks crowd player, with weak aircraft height cues.

view-21.png.evidence: Sharp pale player edging improves contrast against olive ground, and darker varied trees have grounded shadows. A yard fragment adds context but little visible structure in this crop; grass and shoreline still repeat.

view-22.png.evidence: Long wake and tan planked deck keep carrier identifiable within the swarm. Light aircraft on light deck and soft edges increase local ambiguity; dotted effects and stern overlap still obscure player.

view-23.png.evidence: Crisp aircraft, long wake and planked carrier improve surface detail. Continuous light deck reduces separation of pale planes over the runway; crowded stern and generic soft particles remain unresolved.

view-24.png.evidence: Wet road reflections, rubble, rain, smoke and glowing projectiles create coherent storm lighting. Dark tanks and tiny infantry merge with complex ground.

view-25.png.evidence: Crisp hangars, tree shadows, rocks, sea flecks and warmer grass give coast readable depth. Large open ground remains plain, nearby stones compete slightly with plane, and beach is uniform.

general_findings: The service yard in03/06 is a substantive terrain-structure improvement: tracks, fence and distinct equipment supply a functional space rather than just texture. Richness rises, though soft rendering limits detail in03.
A pale player edge improves separation on olive land in07/21, but stern overlap and swarm ambiguity remain in carrier scenes. Static inspection cannot establish persistence during motion.

Continuous lighter tan decks read consistently as planked surfaces, but pale aircraft have reduced contrast when crossing them; broader light deck surfaces also appear less materially separated. No across-the-board score gain is justified.
Long carrier wakes remain visible and coherent in all carrier scenes, but still look like simple twin streaks with limited hull-edge foam.
Environment and lighting still trail the reference scenes through repetitive geometry, limited localized lighting and occlusion, and generic action particles.
regressions: Light aircraft against the lighter full-width carrier deck lose some contrast in05/09/22/23.
Muted trees integrate with terrain but reduce tree-to-ground color separation; shadows carry much of their legibility.
New fine props are harder to distinguish in the soft variant03; detail alone does not fix rendering clarity.
recommendations: Keep the functional service yard and add a few irregular vegetation/shore clusters rather than more evenly spaced props.
Use selective shadow or material variation under deck traffic while preserving planks; avoid uniformly bright deck values behind pale planes.
Apply a consistent restrained player outline through carrier overlap and dense aircraft scenes, then verify in motion.
Build hull-edge contact foam into the long wake and give impacts a hot core, directed fragments and substantial fading smoke instead of diffuse dots.
Strengthen local contact shadows and material-specific highlights on roof walls, equipment and carrier island before adding more surface noise.
